title: Scheme tests for dense open substacks, normality and scalar normalization charts
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use fibred groupoids, stacks and their 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. A morphism $j:\mathcal U\to\mathcal X$ is a dense open immersion if each scheme base change is represented by an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and that open immersion has dense image for every etale scheme chart of $\mathcal X$. A stack is normal if every etale scheme chart has stalks that are integrally closed domains. Use the scheme-base-change and etale-map tests in [def-sfb-moduli-chart-normalization].

For a field $k$ [def-weil-field] and a cover map $v:\mathcal V\to\mathcal X$, scalar compatibility of its normalization charts means the following. For every normal finite-type etale scheme chart $T\to\mathcal X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], every scheme representative $p:E\to T$ of $T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal V$ with $p$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, every field extension $k'/k$, and every Cartesian square $T'=T\times_k k'$, let $E'=E\times_TT'$. There is an isomorphism from the relative normalization of $T'$ in $E'$ to $T'\times_T\operatorname{Norm}_T(E)$, over $T'$, whose composite with the first projection, on $E'$, is the pullback of the specified map $E\to\operatorname{Norm}_T(E)$. Relative normalization and its map from the cover are those of [def-sfb-moduli-chart-normalization].
